item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 171723
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sat Oct 17 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Trudy, located a couple of hundred miles west of Acapulco, Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression is likely to form during the latter half of
next week while it moves generally westward to west-northwestward
over the eastern and central portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Public Advisory Number 17a
item.description:
Issued at 1200 PM CST Sat Oct 17 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 171742
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 17A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
1200 PM CST Sat Oct 17 2026
 
...TRUDY CONTINUING NORTHWESTWARD WITH LITTLE CHANGE IN STRENGTH...
...FORECAST TO PASS NEAR THE COAST OF WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO TONIGHT 
AND SUNDAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 PM CST...1800 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.0N 104.3W
ABOUT 140 MI...220 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 290 MI...465 KM W OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...979 MB...28.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:

None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo northward to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from south of Manzanillo to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from south of Manzanillo to Zihuatanejo
* The coast of Mexico from north of Cabo Corrientes to San Blas
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued 36
hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours before
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds,
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue to monitor the progress of Trudy. Additional watches or
warnings will likely be required today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor products 
issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 PM CST (1800 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 17.0 North, longitude 104.3 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h), and this general motion 
is forecast to continue through Sunday. On the forecast track, the 
center of Trudy will approach the coast of southwestern and 
west-central Mexico this afternoon and pass near the coast tonight 
and Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some strengthening is possible today, followed by weakening 
beginning on Sunday. An Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft 
is currently enroute to investigate Trudy.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140
miles (220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 979 mb (28.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the Hurricane Warning
area by tonight, with tropical storm conditions spreading across the
area today. Tropical storm conditions are expected within the
Tropical Storm Warning area today. Hurricane conditions are possible
in the Hurricane Watch area by late today. Tropical storm conditions
are possible in the Tropical Storm Watch area by Sunday or Sunday 
night.
 
RAINFALL: Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8 inches with isolated 
higher totals around 12 inches along and near the southwest Mexican 
coast in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along 
steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inches 
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest 
Mexican coast in Guerrero and Nayarit. This rainfall may result in 
localized flash flooding, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: Coastal flooding from storm surge is possible in areas
of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by
large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast
of southwestern Mexico and will spread northward toward west-central
Mexico. These swells will cause life-threatening surf and rip 
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather 
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Sat Oct 17 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 171438
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 AM CST Sat Oct 17 2026

Trudy is slowly becoming better organized. The hurricane is 
producing a large central dense overcast with cloud tops colder than 
-80C, and curved bands of overshooting tops in the CDO indicate an 
eyewall is present underneath it. The various satellite intensity 
estimates are starting to increase, but not enough yet to support 
raising the intensity. Thus, the initial intensity remains 80 kt.

The hurricane is moving a little faster toward the northwest, 325/9 
kt. A continued northwestward motion is expected during the next day 
or so as a weak low- to mid-level ridge builds over eastern Mexico. 
This general motion should continue for the next 36 h or so, 
bringing the center of Trudy very close to the coast of west-central 
Mexico. Thereafter, as Trudy weakens and becomes steered mainly by 
low-level flow, a turn toward the west and west-northwest is 
expected, taking the cyclone away from the coast. The new track 
forecast has only minor adjustments from the previous forecast, with 
the center making its closest approach to the coast of Mexico around 
36-48 h.

Now that Trudy is over water with a higher oceanic heat content, 
some strengthening is possible. However, moderate vertical shear, 
dry air entrainment, and increasing land interaction could limit how 
much strengthening may occur. After 24 h or so, increasing 
southwesterly shear and decreasing mid-level moisture near the 
cyclone are likely to cause steady to rapid weakening even when the 
center would be moving away from the coast of Mexico. Current 
expectations are that the system will stop producing convection 
between 72-96 h and decay to a remnant low pressure, and the global 
models forecast the circulation to weaken to a trough by 120 h. The 
new intensity forecast has some tweaks from the previous forecast, 
and it lies near the upper edge of the intensity guidance envelope.
 
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Trudy could strengthen some during the next 12 hours or so as it 
approaches the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this 
weekend, bringing an increasing risk of storm surge, damaging winds, 
and flooding rain. Hurricane Warnings and Watches, as well as 
Tropical Storm Warnings and Watches, are currently in effect for 
portions of the coast, and additional watches and warnings may be 
required.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest 
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Nayarit through the weekend. This 
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides this 
weekend along and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, 
Colima, and Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
3. Large swells are affecting portions of the coast of southwestern
Mexico and will spread northward through the weekend, causing
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
